subject.title: Claude CLI usage probe mints a new empty account session per probe, polluting the claude.ai session list (dozens of <host>-<word>-<word> entries)

question: Should CodexBar keep the Claude CLI fallback by reusing an account-scoped probe session, or disable/opt in that fallback until Anthropic provides a verified ephemeral usage-probe path?
rationale: Both choices affect provider availability and remote account state, and repository policy requires explicit sign-off for provider authentication, remote data handling, and privacy-sensitive behavior.

options.title: Reuse one scoped session
options.body: Keep CLI usage fallback but derive and reuse a probe-only session identifier scoped to the active Claude credential, with upgrade and account-switch tests.

options.title: Disable passive CLI probing
options.body: Stop automatic interactive CLI launches and require OAuth or explicit user action, avoiding remote session creation at the cost of reduced fallback coverage.

options.title: Document current behavior
options.body: Retain the current launch behavior but clearly disclose the generated sessions, which reduces confusion without preventing account-list pollution or rate-limit use.

recommendation.title: Reuse one scoped session
recommendation.body: Keep CLI usage fallback but derive and reuse a probe-only session identifier scoped to the active Claude credential, with upgrade and account-switch tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes Claude provider fallback behavior and remote account-state handling, areas reserved for explicit project sign-off.
